svg.title: Master Theorem Cases and Akra-Bazzi Unequal-Split Recursion Trees
svg.desc: Animated step-by-step comparison of Master Theorem Case 1 (leaf-heavy), Case 2 (balanced levels), Case 3 (root-heavy with regularity), and the Akra-Bazzi unequal-split recurrence tree showing level work distribution.
svg.text: Solving Recurrences: Master Theorem (3 Cases) & Akra-Bazzi Method
Comparing non-recursive work f(n) against watershed n^(log_b a) across recursion-tree levels j = 0 .. log_b(n) - 1
Condition: f(n) = O(n^(log_b a - ε)) for constant ε > 0
Level cost a^j·f(n/b^j) grows geometrically with ratio b^ε; series is dominated by last term.
2. Case 2 — Balanced Levels (Merge Sort: T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n)
Condition: f(n) = Θ(n^(log_b a) · log^k n) for k ≥ 0 (CLRS 4e)
Each of the log_b(n) levels contributes equally. Note: k < 0 (e.g. n / log n) is a gap case.
Result: T(n) = Θ(n^(log_b a) · log^(k+1) n) [k=0 ⇒ Θ(n log n)]
Condition: f(n) = Ω(n^(log_b a + ε)) AND a·f(n/b) ≤ c·f(n), c < 1
Regularity rules out oscillating f(n) = n^(1+ε)(2 + sin n) that break geometric decay.
4. Akra-Bazzi Unequal Splits: T(n) = T(n/3) + T(2n/3) + n
Formula: T(x) = Θ( x^p · (1 + ∫_1^x g(u) / u^(p+1) du) )
For T(n/2)+T(n/4)+n: (1/2)^p + (1/4)^p = 1 gives p ≈ 0.694 < 1 ⇒ root dominates: T(n) = Θ(n).
Handles arbitrary unequal subproblems where Master Theorem fails
